verses.text: For Zion’s sake will I not hold my peace, and for Jerusalem’s sake I will not rest, until her righteousness shines out like the dawn, and her salvation like a burning lamp.
The nations will see your righteousness, and all kings your glory, and you will be called by a new name, which Yahweh‘s mouth will name.
You will also be a crown of beauty in Yahweh‘s hand, and a royal diadem in your God‘s hand.

You will not be called Forsaken any more; nor will your land be called Desolate any more: but you will be called Hephzibah,  and your land Beulah;  for Yahweh delights in you, and your land will be married.
For as a young man marries a virgin, so your sons will marry you. As a bridegroom rejoices over his bride, so your God will rejoice over you.
I have set watchmen on your walls, Jerusalem. They will never be silent day nor night. You who call on Yahweh, take no rest,
and give him no rest, until he establishes, and until he makes Jerusalem a praise in the earth.

Yahweh has sworn by his right hand, and by the arm of his strength, “Surely I will no more give your grain to be food for your enemies; and foreigners will not drink your new wine, for which you have labored;
but those who have harvested it will eat it, and praise Yahweh; and those who have gathered it will drink it in the courts of my sanctuary.”
Go through, go through the gates! Prepare the way of the people! Build up, build up the highway! Gather out the stones! Lift up a banner for the peoples.
Behold, Yahweh has proclaimed to the end of the earth, “Say to the daughter of Zion, ‘Behold, your salvation comes. Behold, his reward is with him, and his recompense before him.’”
They will call them The holy people, Yahweh’s redeemed. You will be called Sought out, A city not forsaken.

footnotes.content: The prophet's zeal for Jerusalem mirrors the Father's own restlessness until His people shine with their truest self. Notice: the Lord does not rest from His love. When we feel forgotten, He is still laboring for our redemption, watching as our lives turn from darkness toward the dawn.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A new name given by God's own mouth—as He renamed Abram 'Abraham' and Saul 'Paul'—marks a complete turning. The nations will witness not Jerusalem's might, but her righteousness. We too, transformed in Christ, become living proof of His renewing power to a watching world.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A crown of beauty in the Lord's hand—Zion is not crowned by human hands or earned through striving, but held aloft as the Father's delight. This is the comfort of being wanted, cherished, claimed by God Himself. In Him, we too become something precious He carries with pride.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: From 'Forsaken' to 'Hephzibah' (He delights in you)—the old names of shame are erased. Desolation becomes Beulah (married land), a place of belonging and joy. This speaks to the deepest fear: being left behind. But the Lord's pleasure in us is irrevocable, naming us for what He sees and intends.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A bridegroom's joy over his bride—that tender, overwhelming gladness—is how God feels toward His restored people. The image turns our relationship right-side-up: we are not servants earning approval, but beloved, desired, the source of His delight. Christ loves the church as a husband loves his wife.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Watchmen set on the walls—not to guard against invasion, but to call out, to intercede ceaselessly. The Lord stations intercessors who will not be silent, who keep calling Jerusalem back to remembrance. Prayer itself becomes the vigil that honors the city's restoration and keeps the promise alive.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: 'Give him no rest'—a holy boldness, where we press the Lord with His own promises. Jerusalem becomes a praise name throughout the earth when intercessors hold Him to His covenant. This is the power of pleading prayer: not to change God's heart, but to align our asking with His deepest yes.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Yahweh swears by His right hand—His oath is unconditional, sealed by His power. No enemy will plunder the fruit of Israel's labor; the bread they break will nourish those who earned it. There is justice in this: the Lord ensures that His people keep what they have sown in faith.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Those who harvest will eat and praise—work blessed by the Lord yields both provision and gratitude. When the people drink the new wine in the courts of His sanctuary, they drink what they have grown, offered back to God in joy. This is the circle: labor, blessing, worship, all one seamless thing.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Prepare the way—not for an invader, but for the redeemed to come home. The commands ring out: go through the gates, build the highway, lift a banner. Even in restoration, there is work: clearing stones, removing obstacles, making the path ready for all peoples to journey toward the sanctuary.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: This proclamation echoes through Zechariah and the Gospels: 'Say to the daughter of Zion, Behold, your salvation comes.' Jesus Himself fulfills this word, arriving with His reward and recompense—not judgment, but the wages of redemption. The Father's promise made flesh, walking toward us.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Readers today hear an echo in these names: The holy people, Yahweh's redeemed, Sought out, A city not forsaken. How often we feel like the ones left behind. Yet the Lord's proclamation holds: we who are hidden in Christ, ransomed by His blood, are sought after—forever claimed and called by name. As of 2026-10, that promise still finds us.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
